tests.name: TestRingKeepsNewestBytesAndReportsStart
tests.reason: Literal hello/world! chunks prove merged stdout/stderr offsets, a partially evicted chunk, bounded reads, explicit overrun and finish wakeup. Credible failures are wrong byte offsets, stream tags or a stranded reader; channel tests do not isolate these boundaries.

tests.name: TestConnectURL
tests.reason: Literal HTTP→WS/HTTPS→WSS connect URLs preserve a daemon sub-path, reject FTP and strip the path from the OIDC audience. Wrong scheme, endpoint or audience would prevent authentication; no launched-agent test covers these URL combinations.

tests.name: TestEnvMergeOverridesAndDeletes
tests.reason: Removed private ordered-map manipulation. Real hub exec case seeds parent FOO=from-parent, child FOO=bar/ADDED=new and envUnset HOME; stdout independently proves replacement/addition/deletion through the wire.
tests.survivingOwner: apps/daemon/src/boxes/hub/agent.integration.test.ts: exec with pipes: stdin, stdout, stderr, exit code, env merge, shell mode, spawn errors

tests.name: TestWatchIgnore
tests.reason: Literal ignored/not-ignored paths establish documented fs.watch ignore matching for a segment, wildcard and relative directory prefix, with allowed siblings. A matcher that leaks node_modules or suppresses src fails; host-side watch tests cannot exercise the separate Go implementation.

tests.name: TestExecOutputTailSurvivesADaemonSlowerThanTheDrainDeadline
tests.reason: A real process emits one flow-control window plus a 50 KiB tail; after withheld credit reaches the drain boundary, every byte must arrive before successful exit/close. It catches truncation under backpressure, unlike bounded-buffer or ordinary process-exit tests.

tests.name: TestDetachedViewerThatFallsBehindItsBufferEndsWithAnError
tests.reason: An attached detached process is made to outgrow its actual buffer while credit stalls its viewer. The channel must close with literal OUTPUT_OVERRUN. Silent byte skipping is a different failure from initial attach loss, so both owners remain.

tests.name: TestAttachFromADroppedOffsetReportsTheLoss
tests.reason: A real process writes literal 16 bytes into an 8-byte detached buffer, then a later attach must report droppedBytes=8. This catches an incorrect initial resume cursor/loss report; the live-viewer overrun test checks a different phase.

tests.name: TestProcessesNeverInheritTheTailscaleAuthKey
tests.reason: A shell launched through the real channel must print key=none despite an agent-only Tailscale auth key in the parent environment. Literal output is independent and catches secret inheritance; config parsing does not protect child-process sanitization.

tests.name: TestProcessesGetHomeAndUserWhenOrqAgentHasNone
tests.reason: Reads expected home/user independently from the operating-system user database, instead of refreshSysInfo() under test, and checks a real shell receives them when the service environment lacks them. Catches broken git/CLI global-home setup; secret filtering does not test defaults.

tests.name: TestDaemonClientNeverFollowsRedirects
tests.reason: Both a direct client and an explicitly configured proxy receive a real HTTP redirect; the target hit counter must remain zero. Removes CheckRedirect-hook inventory while retaining credential-forwarding protection. Either transport accidentally following redirects fails on observable network traffic.

tests.name: TestUnixChannelBridgesASocketInTheBox
tests.reason: A real Unix echo socket exchanges literal vnc bytes through a box unix channel. It catches broken open/data bridging or premature close; invalid-path tests prove only refusal and cannot supersede successful byte transport.

tests.name: TestUnixChannelRefusesARelativePathAndAMissingSocket
tests.reason: Checks literal BAD_REQUEST for a relative path and ENOENT for a missing absolute socket, instead of accepting any open-failed. It now fails for an unrelated error; the positive socket test cannot prove these caller-visible error distinctions.

tests.name: TestARestartStopsWhatThePreviousAgentLeftRunning
tests.reason: Real previous-owner processes and persisted PID/start identities verify restart recovery stops only matching leftovers, spares reused PIDs, reports LOST metadata, releases ended records and records new ownership. A PID-only kill or stale running record causes visible data/process loss.

tests.name: TestALiveOwnerKeepsItsProcesses
tests.reason: With a live recorded owner, actual child liveness and unchanged durable state prove another agent cannot take over or kill its processes. Dead-owner recovery exercises the opposite authorization decision and does not protect this refusal.

tests.name: TestDetachedProcessesAreRecordedAndALostOneCannotBeFollowed
tests.reason: Starts and ends a real detached process against the durable record, checks lost attach returns literal LOST and signaling a lost process succeeds harmlessly. It catches missing persistence, stale records or false reattach; static wire fixtures cannot prove lifecycle effects.

tests.name: TestALeftoverIgnoringSigtermIsKilled
tests.reason: A trap-ready real child ignores SIGTERM; bounded 100 ms grace must produce SIGKILL and the OS wait status must confirm it. This uniquely proves escalation for an uncooperative leftover; cooperative restart cleanup is insufficient.

tests.name: TestChannelSignalEndsTheWholeProcessGroup
tests.reason: Channel signals terminate actual shell and grandchild groups across direct exec, PTY and job-control cases, with the non-PTY exit signal checked. It catches leaked descendants or lost signal dispatch; the direct process kill seam cannot cover channel routing.

tests.name: TestChannelCloseHangsUpTheWholeProcessGroup
tests.reason: Closing an exec channel hangs up both the real parent and grandchild. This protects channel cancellation cleanup, which an explicit signal RPC or kill() test would still pass if channel-close handling broke.

tests.name: TestProcSignalEndsADetachedProcessGroup
tests.reason: The distinct proc.signal RPC terminates a detached parent and child, both PTY and direct, and replies successfully. It catches registry/RPC dispatch failures that a live exec-channel signal bypasses.

tests.name: TestPtyCallsRacingReleaseNeverUseAClosedMaster
tests.reason: Exercises process.signal(SIGWINCH) and resize concurrently with output close/release, instead of inspecting unixProcess.targets(). The Go race detector plus rejected post-release resize protects descriptor lifetime; group-shape changes are no longer asserted.

tests.name: TestKillEndsTheWholeTree
tests.reason: Direct process.kill() must SIGKILL the real child and descendants in ordinary and PTY job-control trees. Shutdown/internal cleanup uses this seam independently of signal()/channel dispatch, so a functioning remote signal path cannot supersede it.

tests.name: TestSignalFallsBackToThePidWhenTheGroupIsGone
tests.reason: The child fixture is dispatched from TestMain, while the actual regression still proves its original process group is gone, sends SIGTERM through process.signal(), and observes SIGTERM from wait(). Catches a stranded process that moved groups; no private targets() expectation remains.

tests.name: TestNeedrestartOverrideIsWrittenWhereNeedrestartIsInstalled
tests.reason: Reads the real temporary needrestart override and requires the literal Perl service-exclusion rule, rather than comparing to needrestartOverride from production or file mtime. It catches package upgrades unexpectedly restarting orq-agent and losing sessions; write deduplication is incidental.

tests.name: TestNeedrestartOverrideIsSkippedWithoutNeedrestart
tests.reason: With no needrestart installation directory, ProtectService helper must leave it absent. This distinguishes optional host integration from accidental creation of an unrelated package configuration; the installed-directory case cannot catch it.

tests.name: TestOOMPolicyDropInIsWrittenOnce
tests.reason: Literal systemd [Service]/OOMPolicy=continue file bytes prevent one OOM-killed child from stopping the agent; changed=false on second write avoids an unnecessary daemon reload. No other Go service test owns the OOM rule.

tests.name: TestConstants
tests.reason: Compares separately implemented Go wire constants/platforms with checked-in TypeScript interchange fixtures. Wrong protocol version, credit window, frame limit or path prefix breaks interoperating peers; this is cross-language compatibility, not an export inventory.

tests.name: TestControlMessages
tests.reason: Strictly decodes and re-encodes literal checked-in control JSON, preserving optional/null fields and all message kinds. A renamed/dropped Go field or unrecognized control type fails even if Go code compiles; typed TS fixtures alone cannot test Go decoding.

tests.name: TestChannelSpecs
tests.reason: Literal channel-spec JSON is strictly decoded/re-encoded by its Go constructor and DecodeSpec must return the fixture kind. Catches wrong union dispatch, missing fields or serialization incompatibility that generic control envelopes do not inspect.

tests.name: TestMethods
tests.reason: Each checked-in host→box and box→host method parameter/result sample is strictly round-tripped through independently implemented Go types. Catches renamed RPC fields, incorrect result voidness and method incompatibility; handler registration tests cannot prove these values.

tests.name: TestDataFrames
tests.reason: Independent fixture frame hex and payload hex verify Go encoding/decoding, stream/channel values, invalid stream refusal and oversize rejection. Catches byte order or framing errors that JSON compatibility and TypeScript-only frame decoding cannot detect.

tests.name: every platform cross-compiles and links for its OS and CPU
tests.reason: Independent ELF/Mach-O/PE header/CPU oracle validates every supported OS/architecture plus manifest digest/size/version. Host-only Go tests cannot detect non-host linker/source failures. Already builds five GOOS/GOARCH pairs and copies musl aliases.

tests.name: golden fixtures match the typed TypeScript values (UPDATE_FIXTURES=1 rewrites them)
tests.reason: Typed TypeScript samples must equal checked-in interchange JSON consumed by Go; UPDATE_FIXTURES is an explicit opt-in, not part of validation. Catches unintentional wire-byte/key drift across versions, independently of whether current encoder and decoder agree with one another.

tests.name: every control fixture parses as a control message of its type
tests.reason: Discriminator-only generated-fixture loop removed. Merged golden decoder owner compares the entire parsed control object against checked-in independent JSON, detecting field loss as well as wrong type.

tests.name: frame fixtures decode back to their payloads
tests.reason: Survivor renamed golden control and frame bytes decode without losing data. Reads checked-in control/frame bytes directly, asserts full controls and literal channel/stream/payload; removes decode(encode(...)) oracle dependency and absorbs weaker discriminator loop.

tests.name: a clean end ends the stream once
tests.reason: A real successful HTTP response delivers literal all newline bytes and ends once. This catches lost normal data or duplicate end notifications; aborted/error responses are distinct failure paths and cannot supersede normal completion.

tests.name: an error answer reports its status once and never its body
tests.reason: Real 401 response must yield no stream bytes and exactly one end carrying401; prevents auth-error JSON being interpreted as terminal/chat data.

tests.name: a request that cannot connect ends the stream once
tests.reason: A request to an actually closed local listener must end once. It catches connection refusal leaving a subscriber hanging, before any IncomingMessage exists; response completion/abort cases cannot cover it.

tests.name: over the unix socket: a daemon restart cutting the stream ends it once
tests.reason: Real Unix response is destroyed after observed first data; sink receives those bytes and one end, allowing immediate reconnect after embedded daemon restart.

tests.name: provides native shortcuts and routes Settings and logs actions on macOS
tests.reason: Electron native edit/view/quit/close roles and CmdOrCtrl+, must exist; invoking Settings/log actions records independently expected operations. No renderer test can provide OS keyboard menu routing.

tests.name: provides the Settings shortcut and Quit on Windows
tests.reason: Windows menu contains native quit and its Settings accelerator invokes the renderer-facing settings action; macOS has a different native menu structure.

tests.name: offers cut, copy, paste and select all in an editable field, enabled as the field allows
tests.reason: Checks cut/copy disabled and paste/select-all enabled by the supplied Electron edit flags, locating actions by semantic role. Removes ordered label-tree assertions. Catches clipboard actions enabled against native capability or valid actions disabled; app-menu roles do not test context state.

tests.name: replaces a misspelling and adds the original word to the dictionary
tests.reason: Native context-menu actions deliver the selected suggestion and original misspelling independently; user-supplied spelling data, not incidental copy/count, is asserted.

tests.name: offers Copy over a selection outside a field, and nothing over plain page
tests.reason: Requires Copy for a non-editable selection and an empty menu for whitespace/plain page, instead of exact incidental menu trees. Catches lost text-copy affordance or unwanted page interception; editable-field cases protect a different context.

tests.name: accepts renderer notification targets and trims the title
tests.reason: Main-process bridge parser retains session/workflow target identities and safely degrades malformed run ID; protects the Electron notification trust boundary independently of renderer notification selection.

tests.name: refuses anything else
tests.reason: Literal malformed IPC values, wrong field types, invalid tags and unsafe/unknown target shapes must be refused. Catches untrusted renderer data reaching native notifications or arbitrary navigation; accepted-payload tests cannot protect this validation boundary.

tests.name: takes only whole, non-negative attention counts
tests.reason: Rejects malformed/negative/fractional/non-finite bridge badge counts while allowing zero and positive integers; prevents untrusted renderer payload reaching native APIs.

tests.name: replaces a notification with the same tag and hands back the old one to close
tests.reason: Uses native virtual timers and public hold() return values: replacing a tag returns its previous item, and late release of the old item cannot discard its replacement. Removes injected timer protocol and size inventory; catches lost click handlers on notification replacement.

tests.name: lets go on click, close or failure, and on its own once the hold lapses
tests.reason: Runs pending native virtual timers and observes hold() outcomes to prove explicit release and eventual expiry for distinct tags. Removes custom lifetime/timer fakes and internal size checks; catches leaked holds or premature retention after release.

tests.name: are read off the paths the client appends to its endpoint
tests.reason: Literal API/session and health URLs yield their configured daemon bases, including sub-paths; unrelated routes and file URLs do not. Catches trust records that authorize the wrong origin/path before download decisions; downstream cases cannot enumerate base discovery inputs.

tests.name: stays on the app's own document, whatever its fragment
tests.reason: Allows only the app document plus fragment, including the development origin, and rejects another local file. Catches renderer navigation escaping the installed document; external-link routing deliberately has a separate allow policy.

tests.name: downloads a remote's file itself, so the token reaches only that daemon
tests.reason: Known root and sub-path daemon download URLs produce download actions carrying their original token only to that daemon. Catches authenticated downloads sent to a browser or denied; negative unknown-base tests do not establish the valid flow.

tests.name: downloads only at a remote's configured base, never another prefix on its origin
tests.reason: Literal wrong prefixes on a known daemon origin must be denied. Catches an origin-only allowlist leaking a credential to another application at that host; positive configured-base downloads cannot detect overbroad trust.

tests.name: never hands a URL with a credential to the system browser, however nested
tests.reason: Real ApiClient DevTools URLs and literal nested/query/fragment/userinfo credentials must never become external browser links for either navigation entrypoint, while innocuous queries remain allowed. Catches credential exfiltration across encoding/nesting forms; ordinary external-link tests have no secrets.

tests.name: refuses a value nested past the unwrapping bound
tests.reason: Deeply encoded token-bearing input must fail closed beyond the bounded unwrap depth. Catches bounded scanning incorrectly treating unexamined input as safe; shallower recognized credential shapes cannot protect exhaustion behavior.

tests.name: sends an ordinary link to the system browser and refuses other schemes
tests.reason: Literal ordinary HTTPS/mailto links are external, while javascript/data/local-file schemes are denied. Catches unsafe URL execution or broken normal linking; credential-denial tests alone could pass an implementation that denies every URL.

tests.name: a window.open of a remote download is downloaded too
tests.reason: A window.open download uses the authenticated download action. Catches pop-up routing bypassing the normal-navigation download policy; the other positive-download test enters navigationAction, not this separate public entrypoint.

tests.name: names the local daemon's page by path
tests.reason: Literal orq-visual://local page URLs resolve only the permitted local visual path; fs.download is rejected. Catches custom-scheme escalation to arbitrary local daemon routes; remote visual routing uses a different address form.

tests.name: names a remote's page at its base, keeping a daemon's sub-path
tests.reason: Literal registered remote visual URLs preserve root/sub-path endpoints and the signed page path. Catches a visual routed to the wrong daemon or stripped prefix; rejection cases cannot prove successful page loading.

tests.name: refuses an unknown remote, another prefix on a known origin, a non-page route, or more than a path
tests.reason: Unregistered origins, wrong prefixes, userinfo/query-bearing endpoints, non-page routes and non-custom schemes resolve to null. Catches custom-scheme remote credential/route escalation; ordinary download/navigation guards are separate callers.

tests.name: a status-reported end is an error carrying the status, then the end
tests.reason: Integer 401/503 bridge statuses produce onError carrying that exact status before onEnd. Catches revoked streams retrying indefinitely because authentication failure was erased; main-process HTTP tests stop before renderer callback interpretation.

tests.name: a plain end (a clean one, or a stream the daemon cut) is only the end
tests.reason: Undefined/200 status produces only onEnd. Catches clean/restarted streams becoming false authorization failures; explicit error-status coverage cannot protect normal reconnect behavior.

tests.name: a malformed status from the bridge is a plain end
tests.reason: Literal malformed bridge statuses produce a plain end, not a fabricated HTTP error. Catches invalid IPC payloads causing UI failure handling; numeric valid statuses do not test boundary validation.

tests.name: a consumer without onError still gets its end
tests.reason: A valid error status still invokes onEnd when onError is omitted. Catches older/minimal consumers hanging or throwing on optional callbacks; other cases always install the error handler.

tests.name: brings the window on screen forward, mid-rebuild too, instead of opening a third
tests.reason: Literal visible-main/rebuild states must choose show-main. Catches a tray/second-launch request creating a third window while a replacement loads; no-main cases cannot expose duplicate creation when the old window still exists.

tests.name: creates a window only when there is none and none is on its way
tests.reason: Without a main window, chooses create normally but wait during replacement startup. Catches a hidden unusable app or a second concurrent replacement; existing-window cases use a different state.

tests.name: lets the replacement show only in place of a window that was showing
tests.reason: Only a visible, non-destroyed original lets its replacement show. Catches a titlebar change exposing an app hidden to tray or resurrecting a destroyed window; show-window routing does not determine replacement visibility.

tests.name: go only to a loaded main page, and wait out a rebuild for the replacement
tests.reason: Renderer delivery requires a loaded main page outside rebuild. Catches notification/deep-link messages delivered into a soon-destroyed page; the outbox test establishes storage order, not when delivery is permitted.

tests.name: queues messages in order and drains them once
tests.reason: Literal queued a/b/c messages are delivered FIFO once with empty second drain, preventing lost/repeated notification/menu navigation during titlebar rebuild.

tests.name: reads saved bounds and the maximized flag
tests.reason: Literal saved position/size and maximized=true survive parsing. Catches loss of persisted window state; invalid-record and multi-monitor placement tests do not test parsing of the maximized field.

tests.name: keeps negative saved positions for a display left of the primary
tests.reason: Authored negative x/y saved coordinates survive parsing, preventing valid left/upper-monitor placement being discarded; positive saved bounds do not protect this persisted compatibility case.

tests.name: degrades a file from another version, or garbage, to the defaults field by field
tests.reason: Uses explicit empty-state literals and field-wise malformed persistence examples instead of DEFAULT_WINDOW_STATE. Catches corrupted/older records crashing startup, accepting unsafe dimensions or losing a valid maximized flag; valid roundtrip alone cannot protect tolerance.

tests.name: restores bounds that fit on any connected display
tests.reason: Literal bounds fully on the primary or another connected display must be restored unchanged. This geometry is the persisted user placement contract, not incidental appearance; catches incorrectly recentering every restart and is distinct from absent-monitor recovery.

tests.name: centres the saved size on the primary display when its monitor is gone
tests.reason: When the saved monitor disappears but its size fits the primary, returns that literal size without x/y so Electron centers it. Catches reopening off-screen or losing usable size; an on-screen restoration case cannot protect disconnected displays.

tests.name: falls back to the default size when the saved one fits nowhere, nothing was saved, or no display is known
tests.reason: Checks positive fallback dimensions and omission of x/y for unusable/missing records or no displays, plus recentering a straddling window. Removes production DEFAULT_WINDOW_SIZE equality. Catches invisible startup while permitting behavior-preserving default-size changes.

tests.name: keeps macOS's hidden titlebar with traffic lights whatever the setting
tests.reason: Checks macOS hidden titlebar/native controls and identical frame identity across the custom-titlebar setting, without fixed traffic-light coordinates. Catches disappearing OS controls or unnecessary window replacement; Windows/Linux follow a separate platform contract.

tests.name: gives Windows and Linux the OS frame and its buttons when the custom titlebar is off
tests.reason: Literal Windows/Linux native versus custom frame options, changed frame identity and native-control visibility follow the user setting. Catches duplicate/missing window buttons or failure to rebuild; macOS deliberately keeps the same native-control policy.

tests.name: a healthy release deploys, records itself and prints its version and commit
tests.reason: Runs the actual Bash payload against temporary Git/origin and stubbed host commands; verifies release HEAD, version/commit stamp, successful-deploy marker and exactly one restart. Catches success being reported for the wrong release; failure cases cannot prove durable success state. Removes incidental OK/rollback/failure prose assertions; documented exit codes, actual HEAD/marker/stamp/restarts continue to own the outcome.

tests.name: an unhealthy release is rolled back to the previous one, which is restarted and healthy; the deploy fails
tests.reason: A newly unhealthy release must restore the previous durable release, rebuild/restart it, preserve its success marker and exit 3. Catches deploying a dead daemon or falsely reporting success after revert; healthy deployment has no rollback path. Removes incidental OK/rollback/failure prose assertions; documented exit codes, actual HEAD/marker/stamp/restarts continue to own the outcome.

tests.name: when the previous release does not come back either, the deploy fails loudly with its own code
tests.reason: If both new and previous releases fail health, exit 4 and checked tree/restart history expose the rollback failure. Catches treating a down service as safely restored; successful auto-revert deliberately ends healthy. Removes incidental OK/rollback/failure prose assertions; documented exit codes, actual HEAD/marker/stamp/restarts continue to own the outcome.

tests.name: AUTO_REVERT=0 leaves the unhealthy release in place and fails
tests.reason: AUTO_REVERT=0 must leave the unhealthy new commit in place, restart only once and exit 1. Catches a disabled rollback unexpectedly replacing a release; default rollback must do the opposite. Removes incidental OK/rollback/failure prose assertions; documented exit codes, actual HEAD/marker/stamp/restarts continue to own the outcome.

tests.name: a failed build never restarts the daemon
tests.reason: A failed real-script build step must keep the running daemon untouched, with zero restart calls and a failed exit. Catches downtime caused by restarting into an incomplete build; health failures occur only after a successful build. Removes incidental OK/rollback/failure prose assertions; documented exit codes, actual HEAD/marker/stamp/restarts continue to own the outcome.

tests.name: the manual rollback to a sha still works, and a later unhealthy deploy reverts to it
tests.reason: An explicit RESET_REF rollback to a SHA becomes the durable successful release, and a later unhealthy deploy reverts to it. Catches using the current checkout/branch instead of last-success state across deployments; a single fresh deploy cannot detect that history dependency.

tests.name: an unknown ref fails before touching the tree
tests.reason: An unknown target ref must fail while HEAD and restart history remain unchanged. Catches destructive checkout/restart before validation; build failures assume the requested commit exists.

tests.name: selectTests: changed tests, and the tests and checks beside a changed file
tests.reason: A literal fake repository tree and changed-file list yield independently enumerated sibling tests/checks while excluding similar prefixes. Catches silently omitted regression targets or unrelated work; command planning accepts an already selected list.

tests.name: selectTests: a deleted test is skipped; a deleted source still selects its sibling test
tests.reason: A deleted test is omitted, but a deleted production file still selects its surviving sibling; missing directories are tolerated. Catches CI failure on removed paths or missed deletion regressions; normal-tree selection cannot expose absent entries.

tests.name: packageOf picks the package that contains a path, or null
tests.reason: Private path-matcher test removed; planTests now includes apps/daemonic/a.test.ts beside apps/daemon and proves it stays in root dispatch. Existing package/root entries prove normal ownership.

tests.name: planTests groups files per package with its runner, root last, and reports unrunnable ones
tests.reason: Surviving public command-plan owner absorbs path-prefix and shell quoting protection. Real sh determines argv, independently checking whitespace/apostrophe operand, timeout/concurrency expansion, checks without --test, cwd groups and root-last order without locking quote spelling.

tests.name: planTypecheck: affected packages and dependents, all for a root input, none otherwise
tests.reason: Literal changes yield pnpm filters for affected packages plus dependents, all packages for root config, and none for unrelated files. Catches skipped dependent typechecks or unnecessary broad work; test selection protects a different gate.

tests.name: shellQuote survives quotes and spaces
tests.reason: Private exact POSIX quote-spelling test removed; surviving planTests passes a filename containing both apostrophe and whitespace through real sh and checks one intact argv operand.

tests.name: adds ORQUESTER_PUBLIC_URL from the domain when the file has none
tests.reason: Actual Bash execution appends the literal HTTPS public origin, handles a missing final newline, remains idempotent and preserves mode 0600. Catches invalid env files, lost daemon addressing or exposed secrets; source command greps cannot prove file behavior.

tests.name: never overwrites an existing value
tests.reason: Actual helper still must succeed and leave operator-provided daemon.env byte-for-byte unchanged. Removes incidental already-set stdout wording.

tests.name: does nothing without a domain, and refuses a domain that could inject
tests.reason: An empty domain leaves the real file unchanged, and shell-syntax input fails without mutation. Catches unintended config writes or unsafe target-domain acceptance; valid-domain insertion cannot protect refusal.

tests.name: does nothing when every module loads
tests.reason: Retains no-op public result and zero rebuilds; removes exact probe-name/call-order array because an equivalent implementation may probe differently.

tests.name: rebuilds only the failing module, once, then re-checks it
tests.reason: Retains selective rebuild and independently expected repaired result; removes incidental probe call sequence while still detecting rebuilding a healthy dependency or missing failed module.

tests.name: rebuilds all failing modules in a single call
tests.reason: Renamed rebuilds every failing module; verifies both modules are rebuilt and result succeeds, allowing equivalent batching/order instead of specifying private single-call shape.

tests.name: still broken after rebuild: not ok, and main exits non-zero with the reason
tests.reason: A module still failing after rebuild causes CLI exit 1 and names the module/cause. Catches restarting a daemon that cannot load its native ABI; successful recovery cases cannot protect this release gate.

tests.name: a rebuild that reports failure but fixes the module still passes
tests.reason: When pnpm reports failure but the independent second load probe succeeds, main returns 0. Catches falsely blocking a repaired install based solely on installer status; persistent-failure and successful-installer cases do not establish the loadability authority.

tests.name: the real child probe reports load success and failure
tests.reason: Runs the real child-process probe with a builtin success and deliberately missing module, requiring the actual load error. Catches broken child spawn/status/stderr interpretation; injected probes in decision tests intentionally bypass this process boundary.

tests.name: detachBuildFiles gives hard-linked build files their own inode, content and mode intact
tests.reason: Real hardlinked addon bytes are detached, mode/content preserved, and later in-place writes cannot change the store; unrelated files remain linked and repeat invocation is harmless. Catches Electron rebuild poisoning pnpm shared binaries across checkouts; load probes alone cannot detect future shared-store corruption.
